sentences.text: Arenysaurus was a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid, a type of duck-billed dinosaur known for its hollow and decorative cranial crests.
The curvature of the frontal bone in this species is very well developed, contributing to the structure of its distinctive head.
A CT scan of the holotype skull — the specimen the species is based on — revealed a volume of 126.2 cubic centimeters.
Arenysaurus is considered one of the most complete and best-dated hadrosaurid skeletons found from the Late Cretaceous period.
An exact replica of the fossil site has been constructed in the village, showing the bones in their original found positions.
Fossils of Arenysaurus were found in the Tremp Formation of the Pyrenees Mountains in Spain.
The remains were discovered in the village of Arén, a small settlement with 350 inhabitants in the Aragonese Pyrenees.
The residents of Arén worked day and night to assist the paleontologists during the excavation.
The type species, A. ardevoli, was formally described in 2009 by Pereda-Suberbiola and colleagues.
Arenysaurus was a medium-sized herbivore that likely fed on plants.
This dinosaur could move on two legs, though this mode of locomotion was optional for the animal.
Arenysaurus is classified within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
The genus belongs to the tribe Parasaurolophini.
A cladistic analysis determined that Arenysaurus was a basal member of Lambeosaurinae.
A 2013 analysis placed Arenysaurus within Parasaurolophini as the sister species of Blasisaurus.
Arenysaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 66 million years ago.
The species lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, about 68 million years ago, during the Maastrichtian age.
The fossil record for Arenysaurus spans from 72.2 to 66 million years ago within the Maastrichtian stage.
Arenysaurus was a medium-sized dinosaur measuring between 5 and 6 meters in length and weighing 1 metric ton.
Researchers suggest that the presence of Arenysaurus indicates a connection between Europe and Asia during the Late Cretaceous.
